portfolio:brief.summary: You've finished the cleanup — 15 keepers left — so this week is about putting your last $210 to work outside AI, not more selling.
insights: You closed AMZN, TSM, MU, AMD and TEM this month and the book is down just 1.5% all-time — the repositioning is done, not ongoing.
AAPL is up 10.4% and NET up 9.0%, both still trending higher — those two are quietly carrying the book while the AI names rest.
GOOGL at -8.0% is your worst mark, but you only added shares July 27 and it rose 2.6% today; let those new shares season.
The losses you booked closing AMZN, TSM, MU and AMD offset future gains — just don't rebuy any of them before late August.
Cash is $210, the lowest it's been, and it should be invested this week rather than sitting through the Fed meeting doing nothing.
mix: AI Infrastructure 32%, AI 22% and Compute Power 16% are really one bet — 70% of your money rides on AI datacenter spending continuing.
Add Energy at 14% and it's 84%, because CEG, ETN and GEV exist mainly to power those same datacenters.
For an aggressive double-digit mandate that concentration is a feature, and NVDA at 16.6% is a size I'm comfortable defending.
The real gap is that Tech 7%, Healthcare 7% and Cash 2% are too small to cushion anything — today's $210 starts fixing that.
positions: NVDA is your anchor at 16.6% and down 2.6%, drifting sideways while the business keeps compounding — that is a pause, not a problem.
VRT fell 7.8% today purely on nerves before tomorrow's results; analysts expect about $1.43 per share, roughly 50% growth over last year.
CEG is weak because New York froze permits for large datacenters for a year on July 19, yet analysts still target about $372.
AAPL is your best holding at +10.4% and sits near its high with earnings in two days — I am not trimming a winner into that.
actions: Sell all $154 of GEV on a bounce, not today.
Hold NVDA, VRT, MSFT and AAPL through earnings — do nothing.
risks: Almost 85% of your money is one bet on AI datacenter spending; VRT closing under $290 after tomorrow's results would confirm buyers stepping back.
New York's one-year datacenter permit freeze is a genuine headwind for CEG; another slide before its August 6 report would need a rethink.
scout: HIGH CONVICTION — MRK at $131.49: cheapest big pharma, priced as if the Keytruda patent loss ends the company while the new pipeline keeps beating; buy $110 now, target $165.
HIGH CONVICTION — CB at $362.62: Chubb earns twice, from rising insurance prices and interest on its huge bond pile, and it does not care what NVDA does; buy $100 now, target $430.
SPECULATIVE UPSIDE — TGT at $143.98: hated retailer priced for permanent decline where even modest margin repair re-rates it hard; size $80 only when the GEV sale frees cash, target $200.
